**A second location of this card's defect: the `sqlite-wasm` kind.** From `domain:cli` seat 2 (#22648) · `os-tesla` · session `session_018t6a5rvqPRvEDMCVVW9kYT` · 2026-10-16T10:03Z · ⛔ not a claim, no label change.

- **Where:** `sqliteFilenameFromUrl`'s `'sqlite-wasm'` branch (`packages/runtime/src/standalone-stack.ts`, exported by PR #23862). It strips `wasm-sqlite:` and `file:` and refuses nothing. The `'sqlite'` branch at least refuses a `SCHEME://` URL.
- **`reach:`, measured at the public door** by the #23794 + #23796 dev (`os-dev-report` `6212949127` on #23794, out-of-scope finding 1), on the runtime host over a plain project. `OS_DATABASE_DRIVER=sqlite-wasm OS_DATABASE_URL=postgres://PLACEHOLDER-USER:PLACEHOLDER-SECRET@127.0.0.1:5999/db os serve --dev` printed `Server is ready` and created `postgres:/PLACEHOLDER-USER:PLACEHOLDER-SECRET@127.0.0.1:5999/db` under the cwd. That puts credentials into a directory name. The CLI host's wasm arm yields the same file name by the same rule, before and after PR #23862.
- **What this card's fix then covers:** under an explicit `sqlite` or `sqlite-wasm` selection, the one rule refuses every URL that is not a file path: a `SCHEME://` server URL (the wasm kind today), an opaque scheme (both kinds today). It names the scheme only and creates nothing on disk, on both hosts. Add `postgres://…` under `sqlite-wasm` to the pins.
- The order is unchanged: after PR #23862 lands, on the rule it exports.

File surface (read on `origin/main` `34b740f2d1`; stop on a breach and explain it in the report):
- **`packages/runtime/src/standalone-stack.ts`, `sqliteFilenameFromUrl` and its docblock only** (about `:590`-`:622`):
  - Both kinds refuse an opaque scheme (two or more characters, then `:` with no `//`) on the value as given. A value whose `file:` (or, on the WASM kind, `wasm-sqlite:`) prefix the rule strips is a file, so `file:backup:2026.db` keeps naming `backup:2026.db`, as PR #23861's CONTROL pins it on the URL-classification path.
  - The `sqlite-wasm` kind also refuses a `SCHEME://` URL, as the `sqlite` kind already does.
  - One scheme-only sentence for both kinds, naming the selected kind. The `sqlite` kind's existing words are otherwise unchanged.
  - If PR #23861 (#23765) has merged when the dev pushes, `main` is merged in and the opaque-scheme expression it adds to `detectDriverFromUrl` becomes one module-private helper that both functions call (no new export). If it has not, the same regex is written character for character, and the parity rows hold the two equal.
- **`packages/cli/src/utils/storage-driver.ts`, `sqliteFileFor`'s docblock only**: its "Two inputs reach that" sentence becomes false. The CLI host already calls the runtime rule and re-raises its refusal typed (PR #23862), so no CLI code changes.
- **Pins:** a new test file in `packages/runtime` beside the standalone database-URL tests, and explicit-driver rows in `packages/cli/src/utils/driver-vocabulary-parity.test.ts` with both hosts' answers equal.
- One `.changeset/23863-*.md` (`@objectstack/runtime` `patch`).
- ⛔ **Hold-offs:**
  - not `detectDriverFromUrl` (PR #23861, in the queue), beyond the helper call named above;
  - not `createStandaloneStack`'s directory preparation (PR #23851);
  - not `StandaloneStackConfigSchema` or the boot options (PR #23843);
  - not `inferDriverTypeFromUrl` or `resolveStorageDefinition`'s logic in `storage-driver.ts`.
Container & model: `S`-to-`M` (one rule on two kinds, both hosts through one export, pins on both), `mode:subagent`, `model: TIER_DEFAULT` (`dispatch-gates --tier` on this surface: no path-derived mandate; Clause ② sets the default tier)
Clause-②: no
Basis for the Clause-② line:
- The values this card refuses are ones the published text already refuses. The module header (`standalone-stack.ts`, about `:34`) says "Unknown URL schemes throw — we never silently fall back to sqlite, since that historically created bogus directories on disk". The `sqlite` kind's own refusal says "the URL does not look like a file path".
- Opening `jdbc:postgresql://…` or `postgres://user:password@…` as a file under an explicit SQLite selection is the misbehaviour that text rules out, not an accepted input. This is the same reading as #23765's `Clause-②: no` on the URL-classification path (PR #23861).
- `sqliteFilenameFromUrl` became an export of `@objectstack/runtime` with PR #23862 today, and no released version carries it yet: the Version Packages PR #23825 is open.
- One file name changes answer: a first path segment that holds a colon (`backup:2026.db`) under an explicit selection is now refused, as it is on the classification path after PR #23861. `./backup:2026.db` and `file:backup:2026.db` still name that file, and the changeset says so.
Responsibility: `the runtime's one SQLite filename rule in packages/runtime, which both hosts call (this lane) | the URL classifier's opaque-scheme refusal (PR #23861) and the module header's rule; neither reaches an explicit driver selection, which skips classification | an operator who sets OS_DATABASE_DRIVER=sqlite or sqlite-wasm beside a server URL: a ready server on a SQLite file at a path made of the URL, and on the WASM kind a directory name carrying the URL's credentials (measured, 6213066437)`
Thread-read: 6213663716
Serial constraints cleared: open PRs read in this act.
- PR #23861 (#23765) edits `detectDriverFromUrl`, adds `standalone-stack-opaque-scheme-refusal.test.ts`, moves rows in `driver-vocabulary-parity.test.ts` and changes two comments in `storage-driver.ts` (`inferDriverTypeFromUrl`). None of those is this card's function or docblock. The parity file is shared, so whichever lands second merges `main`.
- No other open PR or `pm:dispatched` claim names `sqliteFilenameFromUrl` or `sqliteFileFor`. Seat 1's #23826 and #23848 hold the migrate commands and `driver-turso`.
- Same-day churn: PRs #23851, #23843 and #23862 changed `standalone-stack.ts` today.
